summary: Source-anchored research for Distributed on-demand game production networks. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Gelato explicitly excludes individual-card sales and variable-card decks; its card packs contain the same design throughout. Its card formats also differ between North America and other regions. This catalog is not demonstrated as a ready-to-order variable-face party-game deck. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-10-30)

Prodigi treats manufacturing, shipping and applicable taxes as separate cost components. Shipping depends on the ordered product, destination and shipping speed; a product-only price is not a landed US quote. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Gelato acknowledges that suppliers and region-specific materials can cause slight country-to-country product variation. Its stated objective that these differences remain negligible is a vendor quality assurance statement, not a guarantee of physically identical repeat decks. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-10-28)

Gelato says stock availability, production capacity and logistics affect production location; international routing and customs charges remain possible. Its local-production aim cannot be treated as a guarantee of domestic landed cost. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-10-30)

MTG Proxy Reviews reports one anonymous QPMN order with 200 cards: it describes good printing and clean, consistent cuts, average construction, and slow turnaround and communication. The reviewer explicitly says one purchase does not prove identical quality or turnaround for every order; this is a self-reported single-order evaluation, not a cross-plant or repeat-order trial. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-24)

Gelato warns that matte-paper availability and consistency can differ between regions. This is a paper-category limitation, not a measured game-deck defect rate or proof that a specific deck will differ. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-10-30)

Printify says local fulfillment is not guaranteed and product availability can send an order to another location. Therefore, a nearby network facility alone cannot establish the origin or postage cost of a particular deck order. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Printify describes on-demand poker decks with a common custom back rather than different custom faces. It also lists provider-dependent packaging, so a platform listing alone does not establish identical presentation across suppliers. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Printify warns that mockups are representations rather than exact guarantees, and that equipment and supplies can cause small color and placement differences. This general guidance does not specify card-specific registration tolerances. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Distributed print networks do not establish that a particular deck is produced near a US buyer: Prodigi describes a hybrid owned/partner network, while its playing-card product explicitly lists UK fulfillment. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

QPMN identifies its manufacturing base as Q P Group plants in Guangdong, China and Vietnam; its fixed-game offering describes the same complete deck or defined set for each buyer and different artwork on individual card faces. This is a manufacturer-described multi-plant production base, not evidence of US-local game production or automatic allocation of an identical deck across plants. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Printify’s readable product snapshot limits the playing-card customization to one design on the backs, with standard faces; a different photo on each card is unavailable. Do not treat these products as evidence of variable-face game-deck production. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Prodigi specifies one image per playing-card deck with standard suit faces, coated paper stock and a presentation box. Its playing-card offer therefore does not demonstrate arbitrary custom faces or game-specific collation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

For a delivered-cost comparison, QPMN requires a configured card count, material, finish, packaging, order quantity and shipping destination/method; Prodigi explicitly excludes taxes and shipping from its displayed playing-card price. The cited information does not establish a complete US/USD quote for the commissioned game. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

QPMN instructs customers to check card order, front-to-back orientation, small type and border alignment before upload. These are specification checkpoints to carry into cross-location acceptance, not evidence of measured duplex-registration, feeding, collation yield or finished-deck throughput. (low confidence)

Prodigi describes a hybrid production network containing facilities it owns and external print partners. This establishes a distributed print model; it does not establish that every product is available at every facility. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Prodigi lists its playing-card product as UK-fulfilled: 300gsm stock, a UV-coated surface, 52 cards plus two jokers, and one image per deck. This listed product does not provide individually designed game-card faces. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Gelato states that variable card decks and individual card sales are unavailable; its cards come in ten-card packs using one design. This documented product model does not fit a deck of distinct game prompts. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-10-30)

QPMN identifies production plants in Dongguan and Heshan in Guangdong, and Ninh Binh in Vietnam. These are Q P Group plants, not independent supplier organizations; the statement does not establish US-local production or routing of a particular order. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

QPMN describes fixed-deck games in which each buyer gets the same defined card set. It tells buyers to configure card count, stock, finish and packaging. That establishes an offered fixed-content workflow, not independently measured cross-plant physical identity. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Black Chantry’s January 2026 retrospective reports making cards available through Gamepod in Europe and DriveThruCards in the US during 2025. This is a publisher-operated regional POD example, not proof of an open network that accepts arbitrary party-game specifications. (low confidence)
